purpose: 18 original conceptual teaching blueprints and independent transfer checks aligned to draft seeded generator structures; content specifications only

lessons.title: Reconstructing an unknown beginning
lessons.conceptual_invariant: A change is not a starting quantity. The final amount already contains the change.

representations.concrete: Show a covered starting collection, add a visible group, then uncover the original.
representations.visual: Tape diagram: whole = hidden start + visible change.
representations.symbolic: Write start + change = end; isolate start by subtracting change.

lessons.alternative_strategy: Count backwards from the final amount by the added amount.
lessons.misconception_intervention: If a learner adds end and change, ask whether that would produce more than the known final amount.
socratic_questions: Which quantity describes the whole after the delivery?
Where should the unknown go in the bar?
What inverse operation recovers the start?

adaptive_path.after_first_error: Show the concrete model; ask the first Socratic question without revealing the answer.

adaptive_path.after_third_error: Explain the symbolic method and alternative strategy; require a new problem rather than awarding mastery.

lessons.title: Comparing aligned quantities
lessons.conceptual_invariant: How many more is a difference, not a total.

representations.concrete: Line up two physical stacks of counters and remove matching pairs.
representations.visual: Two aligned bars; the unmatched extension is the difference.

lessons.alternative_strategy: Count up from the smaller amount to the larger amount.
lessons.misconception_intervention: If a learner adds the quantities, ask them to highlight only the extra segment.
socratic_questions: Are we combining the collections or comparing them?
Which part of the longer bar is unmatched?
How could you count up instead of subtract?

lessons.title: Tracking opposite changes
lessons.conceptual_invariant: Increases and decreases must keep their signs and order.

representations.concrete: Move counters into and out of a tray, tracking the total after each move.
representations.visual: Number line with a forward jump and backward jump.

lessons.alternative_strategy: Reverse the process: start = end + outgoing - incoming.
lessons.misconception_intervention: If the learner adds both changes, ask what giving items away means physically.
socratic_questions: Which action increases the count?
Which action decreases it?
Can you reverse both changes to verify?

lessons.title: Groups and factors
lessons.conceptual_invariant: Equal groups are multiplicative, not a sum of the two factors.

representations.concrete: Make five identical trays with fourteen counters each.

Can you draw one row per group?
How can a ten-and-seven split help?

lessons.title: Interpreting remainders in context
lessons.conceptual_invariant: A remainder can require an additional container; quotient truncation is not always meaningful.

representations.concrete: Seat 53 counters in vehicles with seven seats each; leave a partially filled final vehicle.
representations.visual: Draw full seven-seat boxes and one partial box.

lessons.alternative_strategy: Compare capacities of the lower and upper whole-number quotient.
lessons.misconception_intervention: If the learner rounds down, show the unseated students.
socratic_questions: What does the remainder represent?
Are all passengers seated after using only full vans?
What is the smallest sufficient whole number?

lessons.title: Nested multiplicative structures
lessons.conceptual_invariant: A product of three factors describes three nested levels, not two.

representations.concrete: Build three shelves with four boxes on each and five tokens in each box.
representations.visual: Tree diagram from shelves to boxes to items.
representations.symbolic: total = shelves × boxes per shelf × items per box.

lessons.alternative_strategy: Find boxes first, then multiply by items per box.
lessons.misconception_intervention: If a learner stops after multiplying shelves by boxes, ask what is inside each box.
socratic_questions: What is counted at each level?
How many bins exist altogether?
How many balls are in those bins?

lessons.alternative_strategy: Find the unit fraction first, then scale by the numerator.

How many groups make five eighths?

lessons.title: Reconstructing the whole from a part
lessons.conceptual_invariant: A known fraction of the whole must be scaled up, not down.

representations.concrete: Place 15 tokens into three equal groups and extend to eight groups.
representations.visual: Eight-section bar with three known sections totaling 15.

lessons.alternative_strategy: Use the unit fraction: one section = known part / numerator.
lessons.misconception_intervention: If a learner multiplies the known part by a proper fraction, ask whether a whole can be smaller than its part.
socratic_questions: Do the 21 beads represent the whole?
How much is one seventh?
How many sevenths complete the whole?

lessons.title: Unit rates and scaling
lessons.conceptual_invariant: A unit price is cost per one item, not cost times the number of items.

representations.concrete: Split a known total price into equal item-price envelopes.
representations.visual: Double number line showing items and dollars, including one item.
representations.symbolic: unit price = total dollars / item count.

lessons.alternative_strategy: Divide by a common factor in a ratio table.
lessons.misconception_intervention: If the learner multiplies, ask what cost for two items would mean.
socratic_questions: What does the total price cover?
What would one equal share cost?
How can you multiply back to check?

Is the final price smaller than the original?

lessons.title: Distinguishing fixed and variable charges
lessons.conceptual_invariant: A one-time charge must not be multiplied by the number of hours.

representations.concrete: Place one fixed-fee token next to repeated hourly tokens.
representations.visual: Bar diagram: one fixed block plus equal per-hour blocks.
representations.symbolic: total = fixed fee + hourly rate × hours.

lessons.alternative_strategy: Create a table starting at zero hours to expose the fixed intercept.
lessons.misconception_intervention: If the learner multiplies the fixed fee, ask whether it is paid again every hour.
socratic_questions: What is paid even for zero hours?
Which amount repeats each hour?
Does doubling time double the fixed charge?

lessons.title: Position versus number of jumps
lessons.conceptual_invariant: Term n is reached after n-1 increases from the first term.

representations.concrete: Place counters in an increasing sequence, marking the first term.
representations.visual: Number line showing equal jumps from term 1 to term n.

lessons.misconception_intervention: If the learner uses n jumps, ask whether term 1 already contains the starting amount.
socratic_questions: What is term one?
How many jumps occur between term one and term fourteen?
Can you test the formula at term two?

lessons.title: Two unknown quantities with a shared total
lessons.conceptual_invariant: Total ticket count and total revenue constrain the same two categories.

representations.concrete: Start with all child-ticket cards and replace some with higher-priced adult cards.
representations.visual: Two-color bar showing baseline child revenue and extra adult-price increments.

lessons.alternative_strategy: Use the all-child baseline and divide extra revenue by adult premium.
lessons.misconception_intervention: If the learner assumes one price, show how swapping one child ticket for an adult ticket changes revenue.
socratic_questions: How many child tickets if adult count is a?
How much more does an adult ticket cost?
Can both ticket count and revenue be checked?
